Name every service that breached its tolerance individually with the binding constraint and the remediation date.
Present the year-to-date schedule status so the board can see which services remain untested and whether the calendar-year obligation is at risk.
Record the minute reference on each test record and on any accepted residual shortfall.
checklist.done: each test is reported to the committee within 60 days with named breaches, schedule status and a recorded minute reference.

checklist.step: Close the calendar year against full service coverage
actions: In December reconcile completed tests to the service register and list any service with no completed test that year.
For each untested service either schedule and complete a test before year end or raise a formal exception with the CRO stating why and when it will be done.
Produce the annual resilience testing statement summarising services tested, scenario coverage by type, tolerance breaches and open remediation.
Carry every open remediation action into the following year's plan as a mandatory retest scenario.
checklist.done: the year closes with a reconciled coverage statement, a formal exception for any untested service and open actions carried forward as retests.

testing.step: Build the population of scheduled and completed tests
actions: Export the approved annual test plan with service, scenario type, target date, test lead and execution mode.
Export every completed test record with actual date, measured recovery time, tolerance, verdict and findings count.
Reconcile completed tests to the board-approved service register and list every service with no completed test in the calendar year before sampling.
testing.done: the planned and completed test populations are extracted, reconciled to the service register and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the test record to independent execution evidence
actions: For every completed test, retrieve the change record for the test window and confirm the change dates and duration match the test record.
Confirm the change record shows the failover actually executed rather than being cancelled or reduced to a tabletop.
List any completed test with no matching change record, or a change record showing a shorter or different activity, as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every claimed test ties to a change record whose dates and activity corroborate it, or is recorded as an exception.

testing.step: Draw the test sample and document the method
actions: Take 100% of tests that reported a tolerance breach and 100% of tests for services with a tolerance of 24 hours or less.
Take 6 further tests by seeded random selection from the remainder, minimum 12 tests overall.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and rationale so the draw can be reproduced.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all breaches and all short-tolerance services is documented.

testing.step: Challenge scenario severity independently
actions: Read each sampled scenario narrative and the written severity justification without reading the result first.
Check the scenario declared the normal fallbacks unavailable - a test that permitted the usual workaround is not severe but plausible.
Compare the scenario to the firm's own incident history and to the named external precedent cited and record where it is materially softer.
Record any scenario approved by the service owner alone, with no independent approval, as a design-control exception.
testing.done: each sampled scenario has an independent severity challenge recorded against its stated precedent and fallback assumptions.

testing.step: Recompute the recovery time from the raw timestamps
actions: Take the timestamped execution log and recompute elapsed time from scenario declaration to sustained minimum viable service.
Confirm the stop point used was the business outcome at the agreed volume and not system availability - a clock stopped at system-up is a fail.
Compare your figure to the reported recovery time and to the approved impact tolerance and record any difference in minutes.
Recompute the data-loss position from the recorded replication lag or restore point against the RPO.
testing.done: recovery time and data loss are independently recomputed from raw timestamps and compared to tolerance and RPO.

testing.step: Trace the business transactions created during the test
actions: Take the transaction identifiers recorded in the test pack and look each one up in the production system.
Confirm each is either present with a correct final state or deliberately backed out with a recorded disposition.
Confirm the recorded throughput reconciles to the transaction count in the systems over the measured interval.
Record any test whose evidence is screenshots only, with no traceable transaction identifiers, as an evidence-quality exception.
testing.done: every recorded test transaction is traced in production with a correct state or disposition, and throughput reconciles.

testing.step: Test whether the runbooks were corrected after the test
actions: For each sampled test, list the runbook defects logged as findings during execution.
Open the current runbook version and confirm each defect is corrected and the version increment cites the test reference.
Compare the runbook revision date to the test date and flag any correction lagging by more than 60 days.
Record a finding closed with no visible document change as an unsupported closure.
testing.done: every logged runbook defect traces to a corrected, version-incremented runbook citing the test, within 60 days.

testing.step: Age the remediation actions and test closure evidence
actions: Export all remediation actions raised from resilience tests with due date, status and closure date.
Recompute days open for each and flag every tolerance-breach action open beyond the 90-day standard.
For 10 closed actions, inspect the named closure artifact and confirm it demonstrates the capability changed, not that a meeting was held.
Confirm any residual inability to remain within tolerance carries a documented CRO acceptance and a board minute reference.
testing.done: remediation ageing is recomputed, closure artifacts are inspected, and residual shortfalls carry CRO acceptance and board visibility.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the service, the test, the failed criterion and the resilience exposure.
Assign a root cause - service not scheduled, test softened, clock misdefined, evidence not traceable, remediation stalled - and an owner.
Set a remediation date and require a re-test of the affected service where the test itself was invalid.
Escalate any service untested in the calendar year to the Chief Risk Officer within one business day.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date, and invalid tests are scheduled for re-test.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute service test coverage for the calendar year, the count of tolerance breaches and the remediation on-time closure rate.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - against the one-test-per-service and within-tolerance thresholds.
Have the signing reviewer, who designed, executed and signed off none of the sampled tests, sign the workpaper.
Report to the board risk committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository as BMA-producible resilience assurance.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states coverage, breach count, closure rate and the conclusion, and is reported and filed.
